thread:
pranav: Heads-up — ONNX build for llama3c just landed in CI and the canary eval shows weird metric noise on our span-F1. Seen anything like this before? :thinking:

alex_m: Which metric exactly and which eval job?

pranav: span-F1 on summarization benchmark (gold/generation overlap). Comparing pytorch fp16 baseline -> ONNX q4 run, variance is large: runs differ by ~2.5% absolute on the same commit. Not a smooth delta, more jitter.

maya-ops: Do we have identical seeds and artifact checksums between runs? CI claims same wheel but double-checking. ci-bot: "build/onnx-llama3c #432 finished — artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/onnx/llama3c/432 (sha256: b7f3..)"

devon: I pulled the logs, there's this noise in tokenization boundary counts across runs. Looks like occasional token split differences -> evaluation mismatch. grep from eval-runner: ```TokenSplitSummary: run1: 124/10000 mismatches, run2: 312/10000 mismatches```

linh: Hmm could be RNG or non-deterministic ONNX kernel ordering. Does the runner pin OMP/THREADS/envs for ONNX path?

pranav: Runner sets OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 and seeds in harness, but ONNX runtime may use intra-op threads differently. Also saw slight timestamp order differences in batch scheduling.

alex_m: Quick triage plan: 1) Re-run canary with pinned intra/inter threads and fixed tokenization seed. 2) Run pure tokenization diff across artifacts to isolate tokenizer nondet. 3) If still noisy, bisect ONNX graph ops by toggling one optimization flag at a time. Who can take 1? :eyes:

maya-ops: I'll kick off the pinned-thread rerun now (job=eval/onnx-canary-try/433). eval-runner-bot: "eval/onnx-canary-try/433 queued — seeds pinned, threads=1"

devon: While that's running, I'll dump tokenizer outputs (token ids + offsets) for a few examples to s3 and link. If tokenization differs, that's the culprit.

pranav: Thanks. If tokenizer is stable, we then try disabling ONNX optimization passes (const-fold/transpose-sinking) one by one. Might be a kernel precision off-by-one causing span boundary shifts.

alex_m: Agree. Also add a stability check: run the same job 3x in a row under same env and compute stdev. If stdev < 0.2% we can mark ok, else hold the rollout.

ci-bot: "eval/onnx-canary-try/433 finished — status: flakey (2/3 runs succeeded). Artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/onnx-canary/433"

pranav: Ugh flakey. devon, can you upload the token diffs and I'll run a quick script to align spans?

devon: Uploaded: s3://redwood-debug/token-dumps/onnx-canary-433.tar.gz. Quick look: token ids are identical for 90% of samples, but boundary offsets differ by 1 char in ~8% — that's enough to flip span match.

linh: That points to deterministic tokenization or whitespace normalization differences at ONNX export time. Are we using SentencePiece version mismatch in the ONNX build container?

maya-ops: The ONNX builder image used spm v0.1.94, runner uses v0.1.96. I'll rebuild ONNX artifacts with v0.1.96 and re-run.

pranav: Good. If rebuild with matching spm fixes it, we should add a strict dependency check in the model onboarding checklist and gate the CI. Also consider making the tokenizer binary part of the model artifact to avoid env drift.

alex_m: Sounds reasonable. If rebuild doesn't fix it, fallback plan: pin tokenizer outputs in the eval harness to use a canonical tokenization step (artifactized) during metric computation, so runtime differences don't flip spans.

maya-ops: Rebuild started (job=build/onnx-llama3c/433-rebuild-spm). ETA ~20m.

pranav: Until we confirm, hold the ONNX rollout. I'll open a short rollback/hold PR on the model catalog to prevent auto-promotion.

devon: Noted. I'll also add a quick unit test to the harness that compares tokenization across the runner and builder images to catch this earlier.

alex_m: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread. If rebuild passes, we'll run the 3x stability check and then decide. :thumbsup:
